findings.fact: A late canceled context and a broad reason string erase the original failure cause. INCOMPLETE_OR_OVERSIZE_REPLY includes size violation with nil read error; HOST_UNREACHABLE includes unrelated failures. Both may be incorrectly reported as user interrupt.
findings.minimum_fix: Register cli_v2.go as fourth path. Preserve existing public/private three-tuple callers, reason strings, exits and L01 HTTP behavior; add narrowly scoped private actual failure-cause result used by read-only status. Only errors.Is(actual Do/Read error,context.Canceled) plus this observer fact permits conversion; size violation, timeout, HTTP, schema and identity failures remain errors. No string matching or final context state as causal evidence.

findings.fact: CONTINUATION_READ_FAILED similarly conflates non-cancel transport/read errors; same causal ambiguity exists by source inspection, not separately executed.
findings.minimum_fix: Within already-owned continuation path preserve compatibility wrapper and expose the actual cancellation cause to status. Retain original bounds, ordering, authorization, no-redirect and projection.

findings.fact: ProtocolFaultRetainsOutcome finalizes before sending signal; it does not cover protocol failure accepted then signal observed before finalization. No synchronized valid-read-success then observed signal before finalization test is present.
findings.minimum_fix: Add explicit synchronization tests for both windows, oversize+late signal, unrelated transport/body error+late signal, actual cancellation, timeout without signal. Do not use sleeps as success evidence. Keep existing actual Windows signal and active settlement assertions.

alternative_exact3: A status-only duplicate transport could preserve cause within cli_stream.go, but duplicates envelope/identity/status/body policy and is larger; fourth-path private cause propagation is recommended. This receipt does not itself authorize edits.
ordering_acceptance: Single finalization with stop/join remains sound under defined observed-signal linearization. A queued signal not yet observed is not asserted to precede finalization. Existing accepted protocol/HTTP errors survive later signal; success before finalization can become interrupted when observer actually accepted signal.
